description: Taking machine learning from notebook to production: the model life cycle, data and experiment versioning, packaging and serving models behind APIs, deployment to the cloud and to phones and edge devices, monitoring for drift, automated retraining pipelines, and the cost and latency trade-offs of online and offline inference. Practised end to end in browser notebooks, simulated terminals and a simulated cloud console, taught to the depth of a strong final-year MLOps course and the machine learning engineering certifications.
modelledOn: Lakshmanan, Robinson and Munn, Machine Learning Design Patterns
Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer and AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate objectives
outcomes: Describe the machine learning life cycle and design a system that connects data, training, deployment and feedback.
Version data, code and models and track experiments so that any result can be reproduced.
Package models in containers and serve them through batch, online and streaming interfaces with tested APIs.
Deploy models to cloud platforms and to low-cost phones and edge devices, choosing compression techniques to meet latency and size budgets.
Monitor deployed models for data and concept drift and build automated, gated retraining pipelines.
Estimate and reduce the cost and latency of inference and design for intermittent connectivity and offline use.

units.title: The machine learning life cycle
topics: Why most models never reach production; technical debt in ML systems; the gap between research and engineering
Life cycle stages: problem framing, data collection, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, feedback
Roles and maturity levels: data scientist, ML engineer, platform team; MLOps maturity models
Framing business metrics against model metrics: a fraud detector for a mobile money operator

units.title: Experiment tracking and versioning
topics: Reproducibility: random seeds, environment pinning, deterministic training, lock files
Data versioning with DVC and content-addressed storage; dataset snapshots and lineage
Experiment tracking with MLflow: parameters, metrics, artefacts, comparing runs
Model registries: model versions, stages, approvals and model cards
Feature stores: offline and online features, point-in-time correctness and training-serving skew

units.title: Packaging and serving models
topics: Serialising models: pickle and its risks, ONNX, TorchScript, SavedModel
Serving a model behind a REST API with FastAPI; input validation, schemas and error handling
Containerising the model server with Docker; health checks, configuration and image size
Batch, online and streaming inference; dedicated serving frameworks and model servers
Testing ML code: unit tests for features, model behaviour tests, contract tests for the API

units.title: Deployment on cloud and on device
topics: Cloud deployment options: virtual machines, managed endpoints, Kubernetes, serverless functions
Release strategies: shadow deployment, canary releases, blue-green, A/B tests and interleaving
Model compression: quantisation, pruning, knowledge distillation; measuring accuracy loss
On-device inference with TensorFlow Lite and ONNX Runtime on low-cost Android phones; WebAssembly and WebGPU in the browser
A crop disease classifier that works offline on a farmer's phone and syncs results when connectivity returns

units.title: Automated retraining pipelines
topics: CI/CD for ML: continuous integration of code and data, continuous training, continuous delivery of models
Pipeline orchestration: directed acyclic graphs, Airflow, Kubeflow Pipelines; idempotent steps and caching
Triggers for retraining: schedules, data volume, performance drops; validation gates and human approval
Data validation: schema checks, expectations, anomaly detection on incoming data
Rollback and model governance: audit trails, reproducible builds and sign-off

units.title: Monitoring and drift
topics: What to monitor: system metrics, prediction distributions, input features, delayed ground truth
Data drift, concept drift and label shift; seasonal effects such as harvest cycles and festive spending
Detecting drift: population stability index, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, Jensen-Shannon divergence, windowed statistics
Observability stack for models: logging predictions, dashboards with Prometheus and Grafana, alerting thresholds
Feedback loops and fairness monitoring across regions, languages and user groups

units.title: Cost, latency and offline inference
topics: Latency budgets: p50, p95 and p99; batching, caching and hardware choice between CPU and GPU
Estimating inference cost per thousand predictions in dollars and cedis; autoscaling and scale to zero
Designing for unreliable networks and power: offline-first apps, store-and-forward, USSD and SMS fallbacks
Serving large models economically: distillation, quantised models, retrieval to shrink prompts

units.title: Responsible operation and capstone
topics: Security of ML systems: model theft, data poisoning, adversarial inputs, supply-chain risks in model files
Privacy and compliance: personal data in training sets, retention and the Data Protection Act
Incident response for models: runbooks, kill switches and fallbacks to rules
Capstone: a versioned, containerised, monitored model with an automated retraining pipeline and a cost report

schedule.title: Why models never reach production
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page case study of a model that stayed in a notebook, identifying three pieces of technical debt that blocked it reaching production.

tasks.title: Take a trained notebook model and list, stage by stage, every missing piece (serving, monitoring, retraining) needed before it could run in production
Diagnose a deliberately messy notebook for hidden state and hard-coded paths, and rewrite it so it runs top to bottom on a fresh machine
Pick a business metric and a model metric for a fraud detector and show, with an example, a case where the model metric improves but the business metric does not

schedule.title: Reproducibility and experiment tracking
schedule.exercise: Explain why a fixed random seed is not enough for full reproducibility, and list three other sources of nondeterminism in a training run.

tasks.title: Pin a training script's dependencies and random seeds, run it twice on different days and confirm the metrics match exactly
Track five training runs with different hyperparameters using an experiment tracker, compare their metrics and pick the best run with evidence
Version two snapshots of a changing dataset, retrain a model on each and trace which snapshot produced a given deployed model

schedule.title: Model registries and feature stores
schedule.exercise: Design a model card template for a crop disease classifier, listing the fields a reviewer would need before approving it for staging.

tasks.title: Register two versions of a model with stages and approvals, then promote the better one to production using the registry's recorded metrics
Build a small offline feature table and show how computing the same feature online at serving time could introduce training-serving skew
Write a model card for a trained classifier covering intended use, data, metrics and known limitations, and get it reviewed against a checklist

schedule.title: Serving a model behind an API
schedule.exercise: Design the request and response schema for a model-serving API, including the validation errors it should return for three kinds of bad input.

tasks.title: Serve a trained model behind a REST API with input validation, and confirm it returns a clear error for three malformed requests
Export a trained model to ONNX, reload it in a separate script and confirm its predictions match the original model within a small tolerance
Containerise the model server with a health check endpoint, build the image and verify it starts and responds correctly inside the container

schedule.title: Inference patterns and testing
schedule.exercise: Compare batch, online and streaming inference for three example use cases and justify which pattern fits each.

tasks.title: Run the same model as a batch job over a file of records and as an online API, and compare their latency and resource use
Write unit tests for a feature transformation function and a contract test for the serving API's response schema
Write a model behaviour test that checks a known input always produces the expected prediction, and show it catches a deliberately broken model

schedule.title: Cloud deployment and release strategies
schedule.exercise: Compare virtual machines, managed endpoints, Kubernetes and serverless functions for deploying a model, and recommend one for a low-traffic clinic app.

tasks.title: Deploy a model-serving container to a cloud virtual machine and a managed endpoint, and compare the setup effort and cost of each
Set up a canary release that sends 10 percent of traffic to a new model version, and decide whether to roll forward or back from the compared metrics
Quantise a trained model, measure the accuracy loss and the size and speed improvement, and decide if the trade-off is acceptable

schedule.title: On-device inference
schedule.exercise: Design an offline-first flow for a crop disease classifier on a low-cost phone, describing what happens with no connectivity and how results sync later.

tasks.title: Convert a trained model to a lightweight on-device format and run it on a simulated low-cost Android phone, comparing latency with the server version
Build a crop disease classifier that stores a prediction locally when offline and show it syncs to the server once connectivity returns
Measure the accuracy and latency trade-off of three compression levels of a model intended for an offline phone app, and recommend one with reasons

schedule.title: CI/CD and pipeline orchestration
schedule.exercise: Design a pipeline diagram with stages for data validation, training, evaluation and deployment, marking which steps need human approval.

tasks.title: Set up continuous integration that runs a model's tests automatically on every code change, and show it fails a pull request with a broken test
Build a directed acyclic graph pipeline with idempotent steps for data preparation, training and evaluation, and rerun it safely after a failure
Add a validation gate that blocks automatic retraining unless accuracy improves over the current production model, and test it with a worse candidate

schedule.title: Data validation and governance
schedule.exercise: Write three schema checks that would have caught a described data quality incident before it reached a training pipeline.

tasks.title: Add schema and range checks to a data pipeline and show they catch a deliberately corrupted batch of incoming data
Set up an audit trail that records which data snapshot and code version produced a deployed model, and use it to answer a rollback question
Roll back a production model to a previous version after a simulated validation failure and confirm the audit trail records the change and its approver

schedule.title: Monitoring for drift
schedule.exercise: Explain the difference between data drift, concept drift and label shift with one agricultural or financial example of each.

tasks.title: Log a production model's predictions and input features over simulated time and build a dashboard of the prediction distribution
Simulate a seasonal shift in input data (such as a harvest cycle) and show how it changes a model's prediction distribution over time
Compute the population stability index between two time periods of feature data and decide whether the drift is large enough to trigger retraining

schedule.title: Observability and fairness monitoring
schedule.exercise: Design an alerting rule for a monitored model that distinguishes a real performance drop from normal day-to-day noise.

tasks.title: Build a monitoring dashboard with prediction volume, latency and an error-rate alert threshold, and show it fires on an injected spike
Measure a model's error rate separately across two simulated user groups and decide whether the gap is large enough to need attention
Wire a deployed model's logs into a metrics dashboard and set an alert threshold, then demonstrate it firing on a simulated outage

schedule.title: Latency, cost and unreliable networks
schedule.exercise: Estimate the inference cost per thousand predictions in cedis for a given model and traffic level, and propose one change that would cut it in half.

tasks.title: Measure p50, p95 and p99 latency for a serving model under increasing load, and decide where batching or caching would help most
Estimate the monthly inference cost in cedis for a model at three traffic levels, and compare autoscaling against scale-to-zero for the cheapest option
Design a store-and-forward fallback for a model-backed app that must keep working through a power or network outage, and demonstrate it queuing and later sending requests

schedule.title: Security and the deployment capstone
schedule.exercise: Write an incident runbook for a deployed model that covers a suspected data-poisoning attack, including the kill switch and fallback to a rule-based system.

tasks.title: Identify three security risks (model theft, data poisoning, adversarial input) in a described deployment and propose one mitigation for each
Review a training dataset for personal data that should have been removed under retention rules, and redact it before retraining
Build a versioned, containerised, monitored model with an automated retraining pipeline and a monthly cost report, and demonstrate a rollback using the kill switch
